title: Неловкие комплименты у ресторана  (Awkward Compliments Outside the Restaurant)

segments.t: Outside the restaurant, Elena spots Viktor Petrovich holding the magazine with her interview and asks how he liked it. Trying to sound charming, Barinov blurts out that she looks even better in the photo than in real life, then scrambles to cover his tracks when she asks about the article itself.
Я вообще-то про интервью вас спрашивала.
А, эту книгу я вообще не читаю.
Now let's go back through the conversation line by line.
'Good afternoon, Viktor Petrovich.' Chef Viktor brings out the contrast between 'good' and 'day' in a few short words. Vika answers right away.
'You have already seen it, huh?' The meaning hinges on 'now' working together with 'yes' in spoken Russian.
'Well, how do you like it?' In Russian, the idea of 'come on' flows naturally into 'for you' without extra filler words.
'Better than in real life.' Vika anchors the line on 'what', while 'life' completes the thought. Chef Viktor answers right away.
'And in this picture even better still.' In Russian, the idea of 'and' flows naturally into 'better' without extra filler words.
'I see, thank you very much.' Vika brings out the contrast between 'I' and 'understood' in a few short words.
'Well, you know how it is.' The grammar packs 'know' and 'really' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange. Vika answers right away.
Я вообще-то про интервью вас спрашивала.
'I was actually asking you about the interview itself.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'I' and finishing on 'to ask'.
А, эту книгу я вообще не читаю.

'Oh, I never read that book at all.' Putting the short word for 'not' right in front of the action word is all Russian needs to make a sentence negative, with no extra helper words like 'do' or 'did'.
'And you are quite right not to.' The meaning hinges on 'yes' working together with 'are doing' in spoken Russian. Chef Viktor answers right away.
'What I meant to say was.' The meaning hinges on 'I' working together with 'say' in spoken Russian.
'And when it comes to hairstyles, he is a bit off.' Vika anchors the line on 'both', while 'that' completes the thought.
'Do not listen to me.' The negative particle sits right before the verb meaning 'listen' to negate the statement. Alright, let's hear the whole conversation once more from start to finish.
Я вообще-то про интервью вас спрашивала.
А, эту книгу я вообще не читаю.
That wraps up this scene as chef Barinov runs into Elena outside and awkwardly compliments her magazine photo before losing his nerve when she realizes he never read her interview. See you next time!
